# JTBD Underservice Finding (Merck 20/20)

The Merck JTBD analysis produced a 20/20 underservice score for this problem
space. That places the opportunity at the top of the quantified underservice
distribution across the 30-venture Merck cohort.

## Why the underservice signal matters

Underservice is the compound of two signals: (a) the job itself is being
under-performed by incumbent solutions, and (b) the JTBD population feels the
gap strongly. A 20/20 score means both dimensions are saturated. Every
[[market-analysis]] run we file against this finding should inherit the
underservice framing, and every [[solution-design]] artifact should explicitly
address the underservice as the core opportunity.

## Cross-section implications

The underservice opportunity is not a standalone claim. It informs the
[[market-analysis]] triangulation of whether the market is still growing, and
it informs the [[solution-design]] choice of which JTBD constraint the solution
should relax first. The underservice finding is the root claim that later
artifacts either validate or invalidate.

## Open questions this JTBD underservice opens

- Does the underservice persist under near-term market saturation?
- Is the JTBD underservice symmetric across segments, or does the underservice
  concentrate on a sub-segment?
- What is the opportunity cost of leaving the underservice un-addressed?

## Summary

JTBD underservice at 20/20 is the anchor claim. Every cross-reference to
[[market-analysis]] or [[solution-design]] in this room descends from this
underservice framing. The opportunity is real and the opportunity is
measurable.
